summary.headline: VMS TMT Q1 FY27 total income rose 16.16% YoY to ₹247.88 crore, but EBITDA fell about 41% and PAT dropped to ₹2.45 crore on imported scrap costs.
summary.overview: Total income for Q1 FY27 was ₹247.88 crore versus ₹213.39 crore a year earlier, up 16.16% YoY, with TMT sales volume and average realisation both stated as higher. Management attributed the margin squeeze to a sharp rise in imported scrap prices linked to the Iran conflict, plus a rupee depreciation effect on cargo bought earlier at lower dollar rates; PAT fell to ₹2.45 crore and EBITDA declined about 41% per the analyst's figures. Billet capacity commissioning and the 15 MW captive solar plant (12 MW live from 7 August) were highlighted as cost levers. Management guided margin recovery from Q3 FY27, with the proposed Aditya Ultra Steel amalgamation presented as a further scale driver.

financial_highlights.change: +16.16% YoY vs ₹213.39 crore in Q1 FY26
Fell YoY (per analyst question; not confirmed by management)
Declined about 41% YoY (per analyst question; not confirmed by management)

financial_highlights.value: ₹228.35 crore (as cited by analyst, referred to as FY26)
financial_highlights.change: Expected to fall below ₹200 crore after Diwali

financial_highlights.value: No fixed debt outstanding per management
financial_highlights.change: Prepaid largely from IPO proceeds last year; financial cost lower QoQ

segments.name: TMT bars
segments.commentary: Q1 production 34,400 metric tons; management says plant runs 20-22 hours across three shifts, with ~80% utilisation of 2 lakh MT installed capacity and a target of 4-5% improvement per year. Average realisation per metric ton rose YoY.

segments.name: Billets
segments.commentary: In-house billet facility commissioned, installed capacity 2,16,000 tons; FY26 billet production cited as 1.5 lakh MT. Q1 billet-specific output and utilisation not disclosed.

segments.name: Binding wire and scrap
segments.commentary: Part of the product portfolio alongside TMT and billets; no separate figures given in the call.

guidance_outlook: Margins expected to improve in Q3 and Q4 FY27; Q2 (monsoon) seen as weak with limited improvement, and faster recovery if the Iran conflict eases.
Sales growth guided at roughly 10-15% annually, with EBITDA and PAT improving; PAT expected to grow slightly faster than sales.

Solar plant: 12 MW of 15 MW live since 7 August, remainder expected within about 1.5 months; ~30% of power requirement covered; savings of about ₹4/unit, ~2.7 crore units per year, ~₹10-12 crore annual profit uplift.
Aditya Ultra Steel amalgamation approved by the board, pending regulatory approvals; about six months post-merger to complete operations. Combined capacity cited as 3 lakh tons.
Management aims for top line of ₹2,000 crore-plus over the next 2-3 years (stated without a time frame confirmation).
capex_capacity: 15 MW captive solar plant: 12 MW operational since 7 August 2026, balance expected in about 1.5 months; long-term target 40 MW with further expansion planned next year.
Integrated capacity: 2 lakh MT TMT bars and 2,16,000 tons billets; billet plant commissioned in the quarter.
Next-year plan to expand installed capacity, timing and capex amount not disclosed.
Current TMT utilisation ~80% of installed capacity; peak achievable ~90% per management.
demand_pricing: Average TMT selling price per metric ton rose YoY in Q1; management cites a premium of about ₹1,500/ton over local players in tier 2, tier 3 and taluka markets.
Imported scrap is 50-60% of raw material, sponge iron 20-25% (sourced from Gujarat, Raipur, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Bihar) and local scrap 20-25%.
Scrap price spike and rupee depreciation compressed margins; TMT prices lagged the raw material cost rise.
Company focuses on dealer-led retail in Gujarat rather than institutional or infrastructure contracts, citing competition and limited supply for dealers.
Dealer network of 227 dealers and 3 distributors under the Kamdhenu brand; network grows 10-15% annually. Aditya dealers in Saurashtra and Kutch to be added post-merger.

qa_highlights.question: What were Q1 utilisation and cost or margin benefits from billet backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Q1 TMT production of 34,400 MT and said the cost benefit came mainly from debt repayment (no fixed debt now). Utilisation is ~80% of installed capacity, which management considers ideal given 24-hour capacity.

qa_highlights.question: What are the solar project progress, timeline, capex and funding?
qa_highlights.answer: 12 MW of 15 MW is live since 7 August with the rest in about 1.5 months; ~30% of power needs covered. Savings of about ₹4/unit after EMI, ~2.7 crore units/yr, giving about ₹10 crore annual savings. Capex and funding structure were not stated.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory rise to ₹228.35 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher-margin products (including 550D) were added, and monsoon-season sales were lower while production continued. Management expects inventory to fall below ₹200 crore after Diwali.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins fall despite revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported scrap prices rose sharply due to the Iran conflict, and TMT prices did not rise as much. Rupee depreciation also raised the cost of cargo bought at earlier dollar rates. Management expects improvement in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Is imported scrap still economically viable versus local scrap?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said imports are preferred for bulk buying, GST simplicity and consistent quality; large players continue to rely mainly on imports, with 50-60% of input imported.

risks_watch: Imported scrap cost and rupee-dollar movement, given 50-60% import dependence and a lag of 30-90 days between purchase and payment.
Monsoon-driven weakness in Q2 and a demand slowdown in construction.
Q1 EBITDA and PAT decline; watch for margin recovery in Q3 FY27 as guided.
Aditya Ultra Steel amalgamation pending regulatory approvals; roughly six months for completion after approval.
Utilisation of billet and TMT capacity versus the guided 4-5% annual improvement; solar commissioning on schedule.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and the merger, but defensive and somewhat evasive on Q1 margin compression, attributing it mainly to external scrap and forex shocks. Answers were often informal and some questions went unaddressed (e.g., solar capex, dealer-network timeline).
key_quotes: So that's why the scrap prices has gone up. In compared to that TMT has not gone up so much. So that is the compressed the profit.
It should improve in Quarter 3 or Quarter 4. Quarter 2 is a rainy season, so there isn't significant improvement as construction remains somewhat affected.
After Diwali, it will come below INR200 crores.
